# Federal HR 2.0 and Workforce Case Management


October 02, 2026


by Jamie Clark


##


#### Key Takeaways


- Core HCM establishes a shared foundation for essential personnel data and transactions, while specialized workforce case management supports complex, policy-driven employee matters.
- Secure interoperability between Core HCM, Tyler’s workforce case management, document management, and reporting tools can help agencies modernize without creating new information silos. Agencies can modernize specialized casework in phases while maintaining continuity, protecting compliance processes, and preparing for the broader Core HCM environment.
- The International Data Corporation (IDC) named Tyler Technologies a Major Player in its 2026 MarketScape for AI-enabled government case management.


Federal HR modernization has entered a new phase. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has awarded the contract for a governmentwide Core Human Capital Management (Core HCM) platform, the foundation of Federal HR 2.0. The shared platform is intended to replace more than 100 Core HCM systems and support a phased transition to a more standardized, integrated federal HR environment.


Modernizing the HR system of record is one part of that transition. Agencies must also plan for workforce matters that require more than a personnel transaction, including intake, eligibility or jurisdictional determinations, deadlines, documentation, approvals, investigations, accommodations, appeals, and regulatory reporting. When these activities remain in email, spreadsheets, shared drives, or disconnected applications, agencies risk recreating the fragmentation that HR 2.0 is intended to reduce.


## Extending the Federal HR Ecosystem


Tyler's Workforce Case Management suite provides configurable, low-code applications designed for government. It supports specialized processes across equal employment opportunity, reasonable accommodation, anti-harassment, employee and labor relations, civil rights, grievances, appeals, alternative dispute resolution, and other workforce case types. The applications help teams manage intake, workflow, deadlines, documentation, communications, investigations, decisions, and reporting while complementing the authoritative personnel data maintained in Core HCM.


##### Explore Workforce Case Management


See how[Tyler Workforce Case Management](https://www.tylertech.com/solutions/public-administration/erp/human-resources-management/workforce-case-management) helps federal agencies connect specialized, compliance-driven casework with the broader HR technology ecosystem.


## Built for Federal Compliance from the Start


Tyler Technologies is a trusted partner in helping agencies fulfill their commitment to compliance with Civil Rights laws, including Title VI, Title VII, EEOC regulations e.g., MD-110, Section 504, Section 508, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. The Tyler Workforce Case Management applications are designed around the workflows, timelines, documentation, reporting, security, and auditability requirements common to federal workforce case management. Examples include EEO complaint processing and EEOC Form 462 reporting, reasonable accommodation case management, and employee and labor relations tracking. This specialized focus supports compliance operations without implying that technology alone guarantees compliance. IDC named Tyler a Major Player in its 2026 MarketScape for AI-enabled case management platforms for national civilian government.


The suite is designed to exchange data securely with Core HCM, identity services, document management, notifications, and agency reporting tools. Core HCM remains the authoritative source for personnel and organizational data, while Workforce Case Management applies that data to specialized case workflows and returns case status or reporting information to the broader HR environment. This division of responsibility helps agencies modernize without creating a competing system of record or a new information silo.


## Modernizing Mission Driven Casework in Phases


Personnel data challenges and relationship-based challenges are two different problems, and when it comes to Federal HR 2.0, Core HCM only solves the former. Tyler helps agencies close that gap, identifying where Core HCM’s coverage ends and casework begins and modernizing incrementally while maintaining continuity and compliance.


As agencies plan for HR 2.0, they should determine which processes belong in Core HCM and which require specialized case management; define how employee, organizational, document, and case data will move securely between systems; and sequence modernization without disrupting regulatory obligations. Tyler Workforce Case Management supports that specialized layer by connecting people, policy, casework, and data with the broader federal HR ecosystem.


The ACT-IAC Institute for Innovation's Federal Human Resource Management Technology Market Research report, updated September 10, 2026, describes ancillary solutions as complementary platforms that extend Core HCM rather than replace systems of record. In its ancillary-solutions overview, the report names Tyler Technologies in HR service delivery and case management, workforce analytics and reporting, and workforce planning and operations. It also specifically cites Tyler's EEO and RA commercial off-the-shelf solutions in the workforce compliance and employee relations category.


ACT-IAC states that its report does not endorse any vendor. Even with that important qualification, Tyler's inclusion illustrates how Workforce Case Management fits the HR 2.0 architecture: Core HCM standardizes authoritative personnel transactions, while specialized ancillary applications manage compliance workflows, case activity, and analytics around that core. Agencies can modernize these functions in phases, connect them through secure data exchange, and maintain continuity for time-sensitive and regulated work.


## Federal Expertise That Shapes the Product


Tyler pairs the technology with subject-matter expertise developed through more than 20 years of managing federal EEO and related workforce case management claims. That experience informs the suite's terminology, workflow patterns, reporting logic, implementation guidance, and product roadmap. Agencies gain configurable software together with a team that understands how federal policy becomes day-to-day casework. This combination helps reduce implementation risk and supports modernization without forcing agencies to rebuild specialized requirements from the ground up.
